Objective\n33\t\n34\t> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n35\t> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n36\t> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n37\t>\n38\t> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n39\t\n40\t- **Static.** No backend. Files on a CDN, works offline, auditable once and trusted\n41\t  thereafter. There is nowhere to upload anything *to*.\n42\t- **Same page, both roles.** One deployment; the user picks sender or receiver.\n43\t- **Screen → camera is the only channel.** Strictly one-way, lossy, low-bandwidth.\n44\t- **Multi-gigabyte.** The requirement that most shapes the architecture (§3).\n45\t\n46\t### 1.1 The honest framing of \"multiple gigabytes\"\n47\t\n48\tMulti-GB support is an **architectural** requirement, not a performance promise. The\n49\tdesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\n50\tBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n51\t\n52\t| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n53\t|---|---|---|---|\n54\t| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n55\t| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n56\t| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n57\t| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n58\t| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n59\t\n60\t> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n61\t> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n62\t> one would overstate throughput.\n63\t\n64\t**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\n65\tand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n66\t\n67\t1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n68\t2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n69\t3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n70\t   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n71\t\n72\t---\n73\t\n74\t## 2. Glossary\n75\t\n76\tSeveral of these words are overloaded in the surrounding literature, and two of them\n77\t(*block*, *frame*) mean different things in different research documents. Everything else is explanation.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Objective\n\n> **A static website that accepts a file from the user and turns it into a visual\n> transmission on screen, which a second device running the same page receives through\n> its camera and reconstructs into the original file.**\n>\n> **It must handle large files — on the order of multiple gigabytes.**\n\n- **Static.** No backend. Files on a CDN, works offline, auditable once and trusted\n  thereafter. There is nowhere to upload anything *to*.\n- **Same page, both roles.** One deployment; the user picks sender or receiver.\n- **Screen → camera is the only channel.** Strictly one-way, lossy, low-bandwidth.\n- **Multi-gigabyte.** The requirement that most shapes the architecture (§3).\n\n### 1.1 The honest framing of \"multiple gigabytes\"\n\nMulti-GB support is an **architectural** requirement, not a performance promise. The\ndesign must never *forbid* a large file, run out of memory, or blow up super-linearly.\nBut the channel's physics are what they are:\n\n| File size | Stage 1 (30 KB/s) | Stage 2 (60 KB/s) | Stage 3 (106 KB/s) |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 100 MB | 57 min | 28 min | 16 min |\n| **1 GB** | **9.7 h** | **4.9 h** | **2.7 h** |\n| **10 GB** | **4.0 days** | **2.0 days** | **27.5 h** |\n| 100 GB | 40.5 days | 20.2 days | 11.4 days |\n| 1 TB | 414 days | 207 days | 117 days |\n\n> All figures are **user-visible file bytes**, not wire bytes. See §13.2 — with\n> compression on, the two differ by 3–10× on compressible input, and quoting the wrong\n> one would overstate throughput.\n\n**Gigabytes are hours-to-days. Terabytes are months.** Three design consequences follow,\nand they are as load-bearing as any coding decision:\n\n1. **Resume is not optional** (D22). Nobody holds a phone for 27 hours.\n2. **Neither side may hold the file in memory** (D20).\n3. **The app states the estimated time before the user commits** (D23). Letting someone\n   start a 40-day transfer without saying so is a product failure, not an edge case.\n\n---\n\n## 2. Nothing in the wire format carried\nthem: the 13-byte header has no room, and the beacon carries only `blockHashLen`.\n\n**A 4 GB file has 21,845 blocks. Even 4-byte hashes are 87 KB — far beyond a beacon.**\n\n**Resolution: hashes travel as a manifest, fountain-coded like any other block.**\n\n| Property | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Transport | A dedicated **manifest stream**, `blockIndex = 0xFFFFFF`, distinguished by `PacketFlags.Manifest` |\n| Contents | `blockCount × blockHashLen` truncated hashes, in block order |\n| Integrity | **Mandatory validation via beacon's `manifestHash` field (§7.2)**. The beacon carries a 4-byte CRC-32 of the manifest data. After decoding the manifest, the receiver MUST compute its CRC-32 and compare against the beacon's `manifestHash`. A mismatch indicates corruption and MUST cause the manifest to be discarded and re-decoded. This prevents infinite E12 failures from corrupted manifest data. |\n| `blockHashLen` | **4 bytes.** Per-block false accept 2⁻³², ~5×10⁻⁶ across 21,845 blocks — comfortably below the whole-file hash's job |\n| Coding | **Fixed K=768 multi-block stream** — `blockCount_manifest = ceil(blockCount × blockHashLen / BLOCK)`, same LT encoder, same GE decoder. They are verified retroactively once the manifest decodes. The receiver reports \"verifying…\" rather than claiming completion. **Critical: blocks written before verification are NEVER surfaced to the user or exported until their hash is verified (I9).** |\n\n**Why not append the hash to each block's payload:** it would make the payload\n`blockSize + 4`, breaking `blockSize = K·L` and therefore D19's entire arithmetic and G7.\n\n**Sizing sanity:** 21,845 blocks × 4 B = 87 KB at 4 GB ⇒ `blockCount_manifest` = 1 (one block). At 100 GB (546,125 blocks): 2.1 MB ⇒ 11 blocks. At 1 TB (5.46M blocks): 21 MB ⇒ 110 blocks. Each block decodes at K=768 (72 KB matrix), so memory stays bounded regardless of file size — flat-cost by design.\n\n**Why the manifest hash is mandatory:** Without it, a single flipped byte in the manifest\npacket would yield wrong hashes for hundreds of blocks. Those blocks would fail E12 forever\n— re-collect, fail, re-collect — with no error code and no termination. These separate because blocks may be decoded before their hashes arrive (§7.6), and they must not be surfaced to the user until verified.\n\nPartial state for a block the sender has moved past is **discarded, not persisted** — a\nbadly damaged block rarely half-completes usefully, and persisting it would defeat I6.\nThe bitmap is tiny: 4 GB / 192 KB = 21,845 blocks = **2.7 KB**.\n\n### 7.4 `streamId` derivation\n\nLoad-bearing: D22 resume requires that re-selecting the same file reproduces the same\n`streamId`, and §3.3 says a full multi-GB hash is not free.\n\n**Derivation (sender):**\n\n```\nstreamId = CRC32( fileSize ‖ first 64 KB ‖ middle 64 KB ‖ last 64 KB ‖ lastModified )\n```\n\nThree sampled windows plus size and mtime. Read all fields (no validation yet)\n * 2. Validate CRC-32 (if this fails, ALL other values are suspect)\n * 3. Then do bounds/K/quota checks (safe now because CRC validated)\n *\n * @param bytes - Beacon payload bytes (after QR decoding and header stripping)\n * @param localKMax - This device's benchmarked maximum K (from GE benchmark)\n * @param availableQuota - Available storage quota in bytes (for T1 fileSize check)\n * @throws {BeaconValidationError} If any field fails validation or CRC-32 mismatch\n */\nexport function parseBeacon(\n  bytes: Uint8Array,\n  localKMax: number,\n  availableQuota: number\n): BeaconMeta {\n  let offset = 0;\n\n  const readU32 = () => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset] << 24) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 1] << 16) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 2] << 8) |\n                 bytes[offset + 3];\n    offset += 4;\n    return value >>> 0; // Force unsigned\n  };\n\n  const readU24 = () => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset] << 16) |\n                 (bytes[offset + 1] << 8) |\n                 bytes[offset + 2];\n    offset += 3;\n    return value >>> 0;\n  };\n\n  const readU16 = () => {\n    const value = (bytes[offset] << 8) | bytes[offset + 1];\n    offset += 2;\n    return value >>> 0;\n  };\n\n  const readU8 = () => bytes[offset++];\n\n  const readBytes = (n: number) => {\n    const value = bytes.subarray(offset, offset + n);\n    offset += n;\n    return value;\n  };\n\n  const readString = (maxLen: number) => {\n    const len = readU8();\n    if (len > maxLen) {\n      throw new BeaconValidationError(\n        'E-META-BOUNDS',\n        `String length ${len} exceeds maximum ${maxLen}`,\n        {length: len, max: maxLen}\n      );\n    }\n    const strBytes = readBytes(len);\n    // Decode as UTF-8\n    const decoder = new TextDecoder('utf-8', {fatal: true});\n    try {\n      return decoder.decode(strBytes);\n    } catch (e) {\n      throw new BeaconValidationError(\n        'E-META-BOUNDS',\n        'Invalid UTF-8 in string field',\n        {}\n      );\n    }\n  };\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ STEP 1: Read all fields (no validation yet)\n\n  const streamId = readU32();\n  const wireVersion = readU8();\n  // originalSize: 6 bytes, 48-bit (original uncompressed file size)\n  const originalSize = ((readU8() << 40) & 0xff0000000000) |\n                       ((readU32() << 8) & 0xffffffffff00) |\n                       (readU8() & 0xff);\n  // payloadLen: 6 bytes, 48-bit (actual payload length after compression)\n  const payloadLen = ((readU8() << 40) & 0xff0000000000) |\n                     ((readU32() << 8) & (CRC-32)\n\n  // Variable fields\n  const filename = readString(BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILENAME_LEN);\n  const mimeType = readString(BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_MIMETYPE_LEN);\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ STEP 2: CRC-32 validation (MUST pass before any beacon values are trusted)\n\n  const CRC_SIZE = 4;\n  const beaconBodySize = offset;\n  const expectedSize = beaconBodySize + CRC_SIZE;\n\n  if (bytes.length !== expectedSize) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-CRC-LENGTH',\n      `Beacon size ${bytes.length} != expected ${expectedSize} (body+CRC)`,\n      {actual: bytes.length, expected: expectedSize}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Read the CRC-32 from the last 4 bytes\n  const storedCrc = (bytes[offset]! << 24) |\n                    (bytes[offset + 1]! << 16) |\n                    (bytes[offset + 2]! << 8) |\n                    bytes[offset + 3]!;\n\n  // Calculate CRC-32 over the beacon body (everything except the last 4 bytes)\n  const calculatedCrc = crc32(bytes.subarray(0, beaconBodySize));\n\n  if (storedCrc !== calculatedCrc) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-CRC-MISMATCH',\n      `Beacon CRC-32 mismatch: stored=${storedCrc} calculated=${calculatedCrc}`,\n      {stored: storedCrc, calculated: calculatedCrc}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ STEP 3: T1/META bounds checks (now safe because CRC validated)\n\n  // T1: originalSize bounds check\n  if (originalSize > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Declared original size (${originalSize}) exceeds maximum (${BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE})`,\n      {originalSize, max: BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // T1: originalSize must fit in available quota\n  if (originalSize > availableQuota) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT',\n      `Original size (${originalSize}) exceeds available quota (${availableQuota})`,\n      {originalSize, availableQuota}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // T1: payloadLen bounds check (same limit as fileSize)\n  if (payloadLen > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Declared payload length (${payloadLen}) exceeds maximum (${BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE})`,\n      {payloadLen, max: BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_FILE_SIZE}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // T1: payloadLen must fit in available quota\n  if (payloadLen > availableQuota) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-QUOTA-PREFLIGHT',\n      `Payload length (${payloadLen}) exceeds available quota (${availableQuota})`,\n      {payloadLen, availableQuota}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Sanity: payloadLen should be ≤ originalSize (compression can only reduce)\n  if (payloadLen > originalSize) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Payload length (${payloadLen}) cannot exceed original size (${originalSize})`,\n      {payloadLen, originalSize}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // T1: blockCount bounds check\n  if (blockCount > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_BLOCK_COUNT) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Block count (${blockCount}) exceeds maximum (${BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_BLOCK_COUNT})`,\n      {blockCount, max: BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_BLOCK_COUNT}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Sanity: blockSize should be reasonable\n  if (blockSize < 1 || blockSize > 10_485_760) { // Max 10 MB per block\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Invalid block size: ${blockSize}`,\n      {blockSize}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // T1: Wire version compatibility check\n  if (wireVersion !== WIRE_VERSION) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-VERSION',\n      `Wire version mismatch: sender is ${wireVersion}, receiver is ${WIRE_VERSION}`,\n      {senderVersion: wireVersion, receiverVersion: WIRE_VERSION}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // T1: L must match wire constant for this version\n  if (fragmentLen !== L) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-VERSION',\n      `Fragment length L mismatch: sender declared ${fragmentLen}, wire constant is ${L}`,\n      {senderL: fragmentLen, wireConstantL: L, wireVersion}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // T1: Secondary sanity check (should never fire if above checks pass)\n  if (fragmentLen < 1 || fragmentLen > BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_L) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Fragment length L (${fragmentLen}) outside valid range [1, ${BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_L}]`,\n      {L: fragmentLen, max: BEACON_LIMITS.MAX_L}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Sanity: degreeCap should be within reasonable bounds (D25 says 64)\n  if (degreeCap < 1 || degreeCap > 256) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Invalid degree cap: ${degreeCap}`,\n      {degreeCap}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // Sanity: blockHashLen should be reasonable (SHA-256 truncated to 4 bytes per plan)\n  if (blockHashLen < 1 || blockHashLen > 64) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      'E-META-BOUNDS',\n      `Invalid block hash length: ${blockHashLen}`,\n      {blockHashLen}\n    );\n  }\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ STEP 4: D26/T1: K validation\n\n  // Derive K from blockSize and L\n  const kValidation = validateBeaconK(blockSize, fragmentLen, localKMax);\n\n  if (!kValidation.acceptable) {\n    throw new BeaconValidationError(\n      kValidation.error!.code,\n      kValidation.error!.message,\n      kValidation.error!.details\n    );\n  }\n\n  // ------------------------------------------------------------------ STEP 5: Sanity checks\n\n  // Sanity:
